response.evidence: Most Hispanic or Latino female applicants in the data were approved. By a manual count, about 14 of roughly 110 were denied (~12%). This is somewhat above the approximate overall denial rate (~8%) and similar to White female applicants (~19 of ~200, ~9-10%). These rates are approximate and come from small groups, so the gap is not statistically conclusive. About half of the Hispanic female denials involve clear risk factors: debt-to-income of 50%-60% or above 60%, reported income of 0 or very low (e.g., 17k), or loan-to-value above 100% (101.85, 113.662). The same factors drive denials across all races and sexes. White, Asian, and Hispanic male applicants with DTI above 60% were frequently denied, and most White female denials also had DTI of 50% or higher. Several Hispanic female applicants with high DTI (50%-60% or above 60%) were still approved, which points away from group-based rejection. The data does not include credit scores or other underwriting factors, so it cannot rule out discrimination or explain any individual decision.
